sections.learningObjectives:
- Define common word parts (roots, prefixes, and suffixes) for the digestive tract, liver, and urinary system.
- Build and decode medical terms for gastrointestinal and urinary structures, conditions, and procedures.
- Recognize common gastrointestinal and urinary conditions by their medical terminology.
- Identify common gastrointestinal and urinary procedures and diagnostic studies by their terminology.
- Apply scope-of-practice and safety judgment when abnormal urinary or gastrointestinal findings are reported.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Gastr/o is the code word for your stomach. If your stomach is sore and puffy inside, doctors say it has gastritis.

### Question 2

Hepat/o is the code word for your liver, the big cleaning organ in your belly that helps digest food.

### Question 3

Enter/o is the code word for the long, twisty tube (the small intestine) where most food is absorbed. It is different from col/o, which means the wider large intestine.

### Question 4

Col/o and colon/o are two code words for the same tube, the colon, which is the wide lower part of the digestive tract that dries out leftover food.

### Question 5

Cholecyst/o is the code word for the gallbladder, a little sack that stores bile to help digest fatty foods.

### Question 6

Esophag/o is the code word for the food tube that runs from your throat down to your stomach.

### Question 7

Nephr/o and ren/o are two code words for the same organ, the kidney, which cleans your blood and makes urine.

### Question 8

In pee-system words, cyst/o is the code word for the bladder, the stretchy balloon that holds urine until you go.

### Question 9

Ureter/o is the code word for the tube that drains pee from the kidney down to the bladder. Urethr/o is the smaller tube that carries pee out of the body.

### Question 10

-ectomy is the code word for taking something out with surgery, like when a doctor takes out a sick appendix.

### Question 11

-megaly is the code word for something growing bigger than normal. Hepatomegaly just means a liver that has become too large.

### Question 12

-scopy is the code word for using a tiny camera on a tube to look inside your body, like a colonoscopy to check the large intestine.

### Question 13

-uria is the code word that tells you a word is about pee. Whatever word part sits before it tells you what is unusual about the urine.

### Question 14

Gastritis is a sore, irritated stomach lining. Gastr/o means stomach and -itis means inflamed, so the word builds itself.

### Question 15

Hepatitis is a sore, swollen liver. Hepat/o means liver and -itis means inflamed.

### Question 16

Cholecystectomy is surgery to take out the gallbladder. Cholecyst/o means gallbladder and -ectomy means remove.

### Question 17

Gastroenteritis is the 'stomach bug' that makes your stomach and intestines both sore. The word combines gastro (stomach) and enter (intestine).

### Question 18

Appendicitis is a sore, swollen appendix, a little finger-shaped pouch near the start of the large intestine.

### Question 19

Colitis is a sore, irritated colon, the wide lower part of the digestive tube.

### Question 20

Dysphagia means food has a hard time going down your throat. Dys- means hard and -phagia means swallowing.

### Question 21

Hematemesis means throwing up blood. Hemat/o means blood and -emesis means vomiting.

### Question 22

Hematuria means blood shows up in the pee. Hemat/o means blood and -uria means urine.

### Question 23

Oliguria means the body is making only a tiny bit of pee. Olig/o means 'few' and -uria means pee.

### Question 24

Anuria means the pee factory has stopped making pee completely. An- means 'without,' so anuria is 'without urine.'

### Question 25

Polyuria means peeing a lot more than usual. Poly- means 'many' and -uria means pee.

### Question 26

Nocturia means having to get up to pee in the middle of the night. Noct/i means night and -uria means pee.

### Question 27

Dysuria means it hurts or burns when you pee. Dys- means painful or hard, and -uria means pee.

### Question 28

Glycosuria means sugar is spilling into the pee. Glycos/o means sugar and -uria means pee.

### Question 29

Proteinuria means protein is leaking into the pee. Normally protein stays in the blood, so finding it in urine is a warning sign.

### Question 30

Pyuria means white blood cells (pus) are in the pee, usually because the body is fighting an infection there.

### Question 31

Pyel/o is the code word for the little funnel inside the kidney that gathers pee before it drains into the tube (ureter).

### Question 32

Urethr/o is the code word for the short exit tube that lets pee leave your body. Ureter/o is the tube higher up that brings pee to the bladder.

### Question 33

Proct/o and rect/o are code words for the rectum, the last short part of the large intestine just before the exit.

### Question 34

Gloss/o and lingu/o are two code words for your tongue, the muscle in your mouth that helps you talk and taste.

### Question 35

Gastralgia is a fancy word for a tummy ache. Gastr/o means stomach and -algia means pain.

### Question 36

Dyspepsia is the fancy word for an upset stomach after eating. Dys- means hard and -pepsia means digestion.

### Question 37

-phagia is the code word for swallowing food. When you see it, the word is about eating or getting food down.

### Question 38

-rrhea is the code word for something flowing out too much. Diarrhea is when poop flows out too fast and watery.

### Question 39

-ostomy is like cutting a door into a wall so things can pass through. -otomy is just making a cut, like slicing a piece of paper.

### Question 40

-stenosis is the code word for a pipe getting too narrow, like a garden hose being pinched so less water can flow.

### Question 41

-tripsy is the code word for crushing something into tiny pieces, like breaking a big rock into sand.

### Question 42

Cystitis is a sore bladder, usually from germs, which makes peeing burn. Cyst/o means bladder and -itis means inflamed.

### Question 43

Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection, a bigger deal than a bladder infection. The word names the kidney funnel (pyel/o) and kidney (nephr/o) together.

### Question 44

Glomerulonephritis means the kidney's tiny filters are swollen, like a clogged strainer that cannot clean blood properly.

### Question 45

Nephrolithiasis means there are little rocks in the kidney. Nephr/o means kidney and lith/o means stone.

### Question 46

Lithotripsy is like using sound waves to smash a rock into sand so the tiny pieces can wash out with the pee.

### Question 47

Hydronephrosis is like a sink backing up because the drain is blocked, making the kidney swell with trapped urine.

### Question 48

Azotemia means the blood has too much leftover trash (waste) that the kidneys should have cleaned out but could not.

### Question 49

Nephrectomy is surgery to take out a kidney. Nephr/o means kidney and -ectomy means remove.

### Question 50

Cystoscopy is when a doctor uses a tiny camera to look inside the bladder, like peeking into a balloon with a flashlight.

### Question 51

Urinalysis is like giving your pee a report card: the lab checks its color, clarity, and chemicals to look for clues about your health.

### Question 52

Hemodialysis is like sending the blood through an outside cleaning machine that washes out the waste the kidneys usually remove.

### Question 53

GERD is like a door at the top of the stomach that does not close tightly, letting stomach acid splash up into the food tube.

### Question 54

Cholelithiasis means little pebbles have formed inside the gallbladder. Chol/e means bile and lith/o means stone.

### Question 55

Cirrhosis is like the liver slowly turning into scar tissue, so it cannot do its cleaning and digesting jobs as well.

### Question 56

Pancreatitis is a sore, swollen pancreas, the organ that makes digestive juices and helps control blood sugar.

### Question 57

Diverticulosis is like little balloon bubbles poking out of the colon wall. Diverticulitis is when those bubbles get red and sore.

### Question 58

Ulcerative colitis is like getting many tiny sore spots along the inside of the colon that keep coming back.

### Question 59

Hemorrhoids are like puffy, swollen veins near the bottom, like varicose veins but in the rectal area.

### Question 60

A hernia is like a weak spot in a balloon where a bulge pushes through, often seen as a lump in the belly or groin.

### Question 61

Melena is when blood has traveled through the gut and been digested, turning the poop black and sticky like tar.

### Question 62

Colonoscopy is when a doctor runs a tiny camera through the entire large intestine to look for problems like polyps.

### Question 63

An EGD is like sending a camera down the food tube to look at the esophagus, stomach, and the first bend of the small intestine.

### Question 64

Sigmoidoscopy is a shorter camera look at just the lower, S-shaped part of the large intestine.

### Question 65

A gastrostomy is like installing a small door into the stomach so a feeding tube can deliver food directly.

### Question 66

A colostomy is like rerouting the intestine to a new exit door on the belly, so stool leaves into a bag instead of through the usual route.

### Question 67

Ile/o is the code word for the final twisty part of the small intestine, while ili/o is a hip bone. They sound alike but live in different places.

### Question 68

Cyst/o is a word with two jobs: sometimes it means a little fluid bubble, and sometimes it means the bladder that holds your pee. You figure out which by the rest of the word.

### Question 69

Gastrectomy means the doctor removes the stomach. Gastr/o means stomach, and -ectomy is the code word for taking something out.

### Question 70

Pyel/o and py/o are like two look-alike words: one names the kidney funnel and the other names pus. Mixing them changes the whole meaning.

### Question 71

A ureterolith is a pebble stuck in the tube that drains pee from the kidney to the bladder. Ureter/o names that specific tube.

### Question 72

Retention is like a drain that will not fully empty; incontinence is like a faucet that drips when you did not turn it on.

### Question 73

Stress incontinence is like a weak seal that lets a few drops out when you cough or sneeze and push on your belly.

### Question 74

Urge incontinence is like an alarm going off too loudly and too late, so you cannot make it to the bathroom in time.

### Question 75

A KUB is like a black-and-white photo of the belly's pee-pipes, taken without any dye.

### Question 76

An IVP is like dyeing the pee-pipes with special colored fluid so they show up clearly on an X-ray picture.

### Question 77

BUN and creatinine are like checking whether the kidney's trash-removal truck is still making its rounds; if trash piles up, the kidney is struggling.

### Question 78

Nephropexy is like using stitches to anchor a kidney so it stays put, the way you might fasten a shelf to the wall.

### Question 79

-cele is the code word for something bulging out where it should not, like a weak spot pushing outward.

### Question 80

If someone reports black, sticky poop, that can mean there is bleeding inside. The assistant's job is to quickly tell the doctor or nurse, like a referee blowing the whistle.

### Question 81

If the pee test shows blood, that is a 'tell the grown-ups' moment. The assistant hands the result to the doctor or nurse, who figures out why.

### Question 82

A kidney stone is like a pebble stuck in the kidney's plumbing, causing sharp pain in the side and a little blood in the pee.

### Question 83

If a patient's catheter is not draining right, the assistant's job is to tell the nurse or doctor, not to tinker with the tube.

### Question 84

Cystoplasty is like a handyman repairing the bladder. Cyst/o means bladder and -plasty means to fix or rebuild.
